chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the dowry, is there a specific time for it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dowry of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was twelve Owqiya and one Nash, and the Nash is half the Owqiya, and the Owqiya is forty Dirhams, so that is five hundred Dirhams.'

key_terms.نَش: Nash (a unit of weight, half of Owqiya)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the timing of paying the dowry and what was the Prophet's dowry amount?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the payment of the dowry (mahr) is not bound by a specific temporal deadline, emphasizing its flexibility in marital contracts. It further establishes the Prophet Muhammad’s dowry of five hundred Dirhams as a normative benchmark, derived from twelve and a half Owqiya, thereby providing a historical and jurisprudential reference for valuing mahr in Shia fiqh.
